title: Operator-lite proof onramp — PRD draft
body:
Purpose
---
This is a working PRD for a minimal operator-facing proof-onramp for customer-managed networking changes (VPCs, peering, firewall adjustments) that need to be recorded, sampled, and optionally submitted to Redwood as compact evidence. Goal: give customers a low-friction path to satisfy audits and support while keeping data footprints and costs tiny for both sides.

Background + problem statement
---
Customers deploying Redwood Private often require an auditable trail of network changes. Full-fidelity telemetry is expensive and legally sensitive. We need a design that:
- captures a verifiable, replayable snapshot sufficient for common audits (change intent, who approved, minimal packet/flow metadata),
- provides approval gates for operator-initiated changes with optional customer consent,
- minimizes retention and egress cost via compact proofs,
- supports emergency rollback/forensics without shipload of logs.

Scope (what this PRD covers)
---
In-scope:
- compact evidence schema (change descriptor + cryptographic receipt),
- approval gate flow and operator UX for private deployments,
- telemetry events required for sampling + retention policies,
- storage lifecycle: ephemeral buffer -> compact store -> redact/archive,
- APIs for customer export, query, and support pull with opt-in.

Out-of-scope:
- full SIEM integrations (we will provide hooks but not ship adapters),
- broad legal/compliance certification (later work),
- deep packet capture or payload-level artifacts.

User personas
---
- Operator (customer-facing): wants a simple checklist and small evidence bundle to hand to internal auditors.
- Platform Sec (customer): requires tamper-evident receipts of approvals.
- Redwood Support/SE: wants minimal info to triage without seeing customer payloads.

Design principles
---
- Minimal: default evidence should be <= 10KB compressed for most changes.
- Privacy-first: do not collect packet payloads; collect metadata & deterministic diffs.
- Verifiable: signed receipts (HMAC or customer KMS) so the chain of custody is provable.
- Opt-in/Consent-aware: customers can choose to keep evidence local, or mirror compact proofs to Redwood.
- Fast UX: approval step should not add >30s to operator workflows.

Evidence bundle (proposal)
---
Fields (compact):
- id: uuid
- change_type: e.g., vpc-peering-add, route-delete
- actor: operator id/email (or proof of role)
- timestamp_iso
- delta_summary: short human-friendly bullet of the change
- before_hash / after_hash: Merkle-hash of the config fragments (helps replay verification)
- approval_meta: approver, method (console/api), approval ticket id
- sampling_seed: deterministic seed used if we sample for longer retention
- signature: HMAC or KMS-signed blob
- small attachments: up to N key:value items (e.g., CIDR ranges, port lists)

Compression & minimization notes:
- Use newline-delimited JSON then gzip. Average expected size: 2–8KB per minor change.
- For larger config diffs, persist only the delta bundle (context hashes) and store full payload in local archive.

Approval gate flow (operator UX)
---
1) Operator prepares change in local operator console/tooling.
2) System computes delta_summary + before/after hashes and presents lightweight evidence preview.
3) Operator chooses: 
   - "Store locally only" (default for highly sensitive customers), or
   - "Mirror compact proof to Redwood" (opt-in, recommended for support/SLAs).
4) Approver signs via console or API. If customer has integrated KMS, sign using customer key; else Redwood signs with customer's consent (audit justification captured).
5) On success, evidence bundle is stored in local compact store; if mirrored, we push to Redwood over mutually authenticated channel.

Telemetry and retention model
---
Events to emit (local agent):
- evidence_generated(id, size_bytes, change_type)
- approval_requested(id, approver_hint)
- approval_completed(id, method, signature_type)
- evidence_mirrored(id, result_code)
- evidence_purged(id, reason)

Retention presets (configurable):
- short: 7 days (default for ephemeral changes)
- standard: 90 days (recommended for auditable changes)
- long: customer-managed archive (delegated to customer S3/GCS)

Sampling rules:
- Always keep 100% of approval_completed events for 7 days.
- For standard retention, sample 10% of low-risk changes beyond 30 days and keep full proof for sampled items.
- Critical changes (route table, peering, default-route) are always retained for standard window.

APIs and contracts (sketch)
---
- POST /evidence (local agent -> local store) payload: evidence bundle (base64 gzipped)
- POST /mirror/evidence (local agent -> Redwood) payload: signed compact bundle + minimal metadata
- GET /evidence/{id} (authorized) -> returns bundle header and retrieval handle (if archived)
- DELETE /evidence/{id}?purge=true (operator triggered) -> soft-delete or purge depending on policy

Security and compliance notes
---
- Signatures: support customer-provided keys (KMS/HSM) via envelope-wrapping; fallback to Redwood-signed receipts only with explicit consent.
- Encryption in transit: mTLS for mirror channel; local store encrypted at rest.
- Access controls: RBAC at operator and account level; evidence read requires dual-approval for Redwood support access.

Support/forensics flow
---
- When customer opts to mirror, Redwood support can request a specific bundle via a support ticket.
- For high-severity incidents, an emergency retrieval flow exists with audit trail and customer notification.

Cost & capacity considerations
---
- Estimate: at 5K changes/month, avg 4KB bundle -> ~20MB/month per customer mirrored.
- Storage: mirrored compact proofs kept compressed; archival moved to cold storage after 90 days.
- Network: mirror cost negligible relative to model egress, but we must budget for peak bursts (onboarding waves).

Open questions & decision points
---
- Default signing model: should we require customer KMS for all mirrored evidence (higher security) or allow Redwood-signed receipts for ease of use?
- Sampling thresholds: what heuristics classify low vs high risk across business customers?
- Legal hold: support for court/legal hold requests needs a later design.

Implementation roadmap (3-stage)
---
Stage 0 (MVP, 6 weeks):
- implement evidence bundle format, local agent hook, approval preview UI, local store, telemetry events, minimal mirror API (opt-in).
Stage 1 (3 months):
- KMS integration for signing, retention presets, sampling engine, Redwood mirror pipeline with authentication and redaction rules.
Stage 2 (6 months):
- Support retrieval/archival UI in Console, emergency retrieval workflow, audit export tooling, SIEM hooks.

Milestones & success metrics
---
- Time-to-approve: median < 30s for operator approvals.
- Mirror opt-in rate: >= 50% of onboarding customers in pilot.
- Average bundle size < 10KB for 90% of changes.
- Support tickets requiring full config < 10% for customers using compact proofs.

Notes to reviewers
---
This is intentionally lightweight and piloted for a set of 10 customers (pilot cohort). Looking for feedback on the evidence schema (is it enough for auditors?), sampling thresholds, and the default signing model.

Next steps
---
- Review with infra-sre for local agent constraints (Jan 24),
- Sync with security on KMS integration and RBAC (Jan 27),
- Create PROJ-9812 ticket for MVP implementation and schedule pilot invites.

Unresolved items (short list)
---
- exact hash algorithm and canonicalization rules for before/after fragments,
- lifecycle for ties to support tickets (how long to retain linkages),
- UX copy for "mirror to Redwood" explaining privacy/security clearly.

-- end of draft --
